AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: The aim of the present anatomic and radiologic study was to evaluate the location, extension and characteristics of the Brödel's plane and eventually define its different patterns.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: We evaluated 15 human normal kidneys sampled from un-embalmed cadavers without clinical history or anatomical evidence of renal diseases. Kidneys with the surrounding perirenal fat tissue were removed en bloc with the abdominal segment of the aorta. The renal artery was injected with acrylic and radiopaque resins. A computed tomography examination of the injected kidneys was performed. After the imaging acquisition, the specimens were treated with sodium hydroxide for removal of the parenchyma to obtain the vascular casts. Images were elaborated using dedicated 3D software to improve the possibility to identify the Brödel's plane. The avascular plane was identified directly on the vascular casts and confirmed on the corresponding 3D images.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The avascular plane was located in all cases medially to the lateral convex border of the kidneys. The recorded mean distance was 2.04 cm (range 1.8-2.4 cm). Three patterns of distribution of the Brödel's line were identified. In 5 (33.3%) cases the avascular plane was extended from the apical to the inferior segment of the kidneys (Type 1); in 6 (40%) from the superior to the inferior segment (Type 2); in 4 (26.7%) from the apical to the middle segment (Type 3). Fourth and fifth order vessels crossing the Brödel's line were detected in all the analyzed cases.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: The renal avascular plane showed a different extension allowing us to clustering three different patterns. Preoperative identification of the Brödel's line patterns could help surgeons to minimize hemorrhagic complications during percutaneous and surgical procedures requiring an incision of the renal parenchyma such as percutaneous, traditional or robot-assisted nephrolithotomy or partial nephrectomy for endophytic renal tumors.
